title: Dire, lire et écrire des messages
summary: Use dire, lire and écrire, with the important derivative exceptions of dire and the écrire family.
objectives: Distinguish vous dites/redites from interdisez and recognise maudire's plural.

sections.title: Dire has vous dites, but not every derivative does
paragraphs: Dire means say or tell. Redire (say again) follows its full pattern: je redis, tu redis, il/elle/on redit, nous redisons, vous redites, ils/elles redisent. In contrast, interdire (forbid), prédire (predict), contredire (contradict) and médire (speak ill) use -disez with vous. Their other present persons follow the usual dire pattern. For example: j'interdis, tu interdis, il/elle/on interdit, nous interdisons, vous interdisez, ils/elles interdisent.

Maudire (curse) is a lower-priority recognition verb with a different plural: je maudis, tu maudis, il/elle/on maudit, nous maudissons, vous maudissez, ils/elles maudissent. It is included to prevent a misleading 'all derivatives are identical' rule. Médire is followed by de before the person spoken ill of.

examples.note: Le stationnement (m.) means parking; this derivative uses -disez.

examples.french: Dans le récit, ils **maudissent** le voleur.
examples.english: In the story, they curse the thief.
examples.note: Recognition example: maudire has -iss- in the plural; un voleur (m.) is a thief.

mistakes.why: Dire itself has the irregular vous form dites.
Interdire does not copy dites in the vous form.

sections.title: Lire adds s in the plural; écrire adds v
paragraphs: Lire (read) uses lis, lis, lit in the singular and lisons, lisez, lisent in the plural. Écrire (write) uses écris, écris, écrit, then écrivons, écrivez, écrivent. Keep the accent in écrire and its forms.

Inscrire (write down/register) and décrire (describe) follow écrire. Inscrire gives j'inscris, tu inscris, il/elle/on inscrit, nous inscrivons, vous inscrivez, ils/elles inscrivent. S'inscrire means register oneself; the added reflexive pronoun is taught next. Un message (m.) is a message; une adresse (f.) is an address.
points: Do not add v to the singular of écrire; do not omit it from the plural.

sections.title: Transfer a known paradigm without confusing the meanings
paragraphs: Relire means read again and élire means elect. Both retain the lire pattern, including the s in plural forms. Keep the prefix and conjugate the familiar base. This is a way to check forms you encounter, not a rule that every verb beginning with re- or é- belongs to lire.

practice.prompt: Use relire for reading a draft again: 'L'architecte ___ son rapport avant la réunion.'
practice.explanation: The singular subject takes relit, on the model of il lit.

practice.prompt: Use élire: 'Cette année, nous ___ deux représentants.'
practice.explanation: Nous élisons has the same plural pattern as nous lisons and keeps é.

practice.prompt: Supply relire then élire in the present, separated by a comma: 'Vous ___ le règlement, puis vous ___ le comité.'
practice.explanation: Both use the vous lisez pattern; only élire means elect.

practice.prompt: Choose the vous form of redire.
practice.explanation: Redire follows dire, including vous redites.
Interdire has vous interdisez, not interdites.
Contredire uses the -disez ending with vous.
Inscrire adds v in the plural like écrire.
No v in the singular; tu ends in s.
The plural third-person form is lisent.

practice.prompt: In a story, choose the nous form of maudire.
practice.explanation: Maudire has -iss- in the present plural.

practice.prompt: Supply prédire: 'Vous ___ la fin du film.'

practice.explanation: Décrire follows écrire, adding v in the plural.
Médire uses -disez and takes de before the person.
Redire retains the dire pattern after re-.

production_task.prompt: Describe three steps in handling a message: reading it, telling someone something, and writing a reply. Use at least two different subjects.
production_task.model_answer: Je lis le message. Nous disons merci. Nous écrivons une réponse.
production_task.translation: I read the message. We say thank you. We write a reply.
rubric: Distinguish disons from the vous form dites.
